output.reason: Reported recurrent seasonal sneezing, itchy eyes and nasal stuffiness without any reported fever, unilateral obstruction, breathing or swelling symptoms can be managed with over-the-counter measures and guidance alone.
output.patientMessage: You can start today with over-the-counter care: a non-sedating antihistamine such as cetirizine or loratadine, plus a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, which takes 1-2 weeks for full effect. Saline rinses help too. Limit decongestant sprays to 3 days to avoid rebound congestion. If you develop wheeze, trouble breathing, facial swelling, fever, one-sided blockage or bloody discharge, or symptoms don't improve in 2 weeks, get clinical care.
differential: Seasonal allergic rhinitis with allergic conjunctivitis
